name: Ts’ao Sung
bio: Ts’ao Sung flourished about AD 870–920. His poem here is a protest against war, written in the sixth year of the Ch’ien Fu period (AD 879).
The poems here are Arthur Waley’s version in A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: A Protest in the Sixth Year of Ch’ien Fu
poems.author: Ts’ao Sung
poems.collection: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918)
poems.text:
The hills and rivers of the lowland country
You have made your battle-ground.
How do you suppose the people who live there
Will procure “firewood and hay”?
Do not let me hear you talking together
About titles and promotions;
For a single general’s reputation
Is made out of ten thousand corpses.
